pages.summary: Single curated link page 'Roux Resources' (568 words, last modified 2026-09-11 by eff). Two H1 groups. 'Roux Resources': General Resources (rouxcubing.com by Knut Peterson, Roux Method Speedsolvers Discord, One-Handed Solvers' Discord); Beginner Tutorials (two collapsible Q&As: already-can-solve -> Donovan's Roux guide or Kian Mansour's beginner Roux playlist; never-solved -> Kian's tutorial or tutorial.rouxers.com, noting Roux is 'a fairly good beginner method'); First Block (Neo's block-recognition sheet, Shadowslice 'Frameworks' doc, Teoidus FB-in-inspection video with note to 'panic find' a BL edge rather than DL, onionhoney FB/FBLP/FB analyzer trainers); Second Block (Kian's SBLP algs + Louis' tricks doc, onionhoney Second Square trainer); CMLL (rouxcubing CMLL alg-resource list 2H+OH, James Macdiarmid 'Better CP Recognition' for recognizing from all angles); Last Six Edges (advice: learn EOLR and beyond intuitively, e.g. a different EO for EOLR, a different EOLR for EOLRb; Teoidus intermediate LSE crash course, Crys DFDB 4c video, Roux Reader dots-avoidance section, onionhoney LSE trainers, Jade's enbyne.tech EOLRb trainer and LSE 'laser' trainers (misoriented-centres option noted broken), Neo's non-<M,U> EOLRb algs; collapsibles: 4a EO flowchart image, DFDB written guide image, EOLR Docs #1/#2 + Optimal EOLR spreadsheet); Miscellaneous (described as 'unexplored algsets/techniques': Straughan recognition / Three Sticker Tracking, TCMLL OH-only, ACMLL, CEOR = CPFB + COLS); Big Cubes (Kian's Meyer 4x4 tutorial, Fengyuan Lou's Meyer pastebin guide, Louis' parity CMLL sheet). 'Important General Stuff': Speedsolving Advice (Charlie Eggins practice guide, Antoine Cantin on planning F2B in inspection, Dylan Miller lookahead guide (CFOP-based, principles transfer), Jayden McNeill on gatekeeping info); Competition Advice (Zucker Abudi on anxiety, Litany Against Fear, 'The old man lost his horse'); Fingertricks (Anto Kam OH fingertricks, Jayden McNeill 'Why you suck at turning'); Reconstructions (reco.nz Roux filter, eff's example-solves sheet, Fahmi's and eff's Cubeast ao100 shares); Roux Lore (Athefre's cubinghistory Roux article, rouxcubing acronyms/definitions tab, Zhouheng's Midori coaching video); Contributing blurb. No original long-form teaching text except the two embedded images and short notes. Site has client-side search (fuse) and a precaching service worker.

pages.view: asset /eo-flowchart.png (Last Six Edges > details 'Edge Orientation (4a) flowchart')
pages.summary: Diagram titled 'LSE Edge Orientation (Step 4a)', split into 'Lefty M Moves' and 'Righty M Moves'. Cubes show only misoriented edge stickers in red. Flowchart: the 6-flip case takes M' U M' (righty: M' U' M') to reach a smaller case; 2-flip/other cases are listed with the sequence that converts them (M2', M' U M, M' U2 M', M' U M'; righty M2', M' U' M, M' U2' M', M' U' M') into one of two final 4-flip states (arrow / four-on-top), finished by M' U M' or M U M' (righty M' U' M' or M U' M'). It is a ready-made spec for a 4a EO reference screen or EO recognition drill.

pages.view: asset /dfdb-guide.png (Last Six Edges > details 'DFDB Written Guide')
pages.summary: Illustrated written explanation of the DFDB recognition method for 4c (author unnamed; white-bottom pictures). Before inserting the LR edges (shown with M2, but also applies to M' U2 M, M' U2 M' and mirrors), determine which D edge (DF/DB piece) will end up on the bottom. Case 1: it matches its F/B centre -> insert LR, AUF so the D pieces are opposite; exactly one matches its U/D centre (3: bottom or 4: top); bring the non-matching one to the top with a quarter M, U2, fix centres. Case 2: it does not match its F/B centre -> insert LR, AUF to solve corners; the top D piece is either on top of the bottom one (5: do M2 U2 to reach 3 or 4, predictable in advance) or opposite it (6: quarter M to put the non-matching D piece on top, U2, then put the D centre on top and U2 M2).
drills: Predict the 4c case before inserting the LR edges (4b), then execute 4c without a pause

notes: Coverage: all 4 sitemap URLs fetched (static Hugo HTML, no JS rendering needed); every file under content/ fetched raw from main (only content/_index.md and content/docs/contributing.md exist) and checked byte-identical with a clone; the pre-monopage content/ (8 files at 4223ed1) was also saved from git history. The live link list holds 49 article links on / (47 unique URLs; onionhoney #fb and Kian's playlist each appear twice) plus 5 on /docs/contributing/ and 2 embedded images. Every external link answered 200 except the blocked/rate-limited ones listed. What matters for Rouxtine: (1) The hub is a link directory, not teaching content. Its value is the curated taxonomy (FB, SB, CMLL, LSE, Misc/experimental, Big Cubes, Speedsolving, Competition, Fingertricks, Reconstructions, Lore), which maps well onto an in-app 'Learn/Resources' screen with outbound links (allowed without a licence). (2) Trainer gaps compared with onionhoney: Jade's enbyne.tech EOLRb trainer and LSE 'laser' trainers (with misoriented-centre scrambles); EOLRb cases that are not <M,U>-generated (Neo's list); 4c DFDB prediction; a 4a EO flowchart reference with lefty/righty variants; CMLL all-angle recognition; reconstructions viewer/example solves; big-cube Roux (Meyer, parity CMLL) if 4x4 is ever in scope; experimental sets (TCMLL for OH, ACMLL, CEOR/COLS, Straughan three-sticker tracking) as an advanced tier. (3) Content to keep Roux-only: the Dylan Miller lookahead link is CFOP-based ('principles transfer'); reuse only generic lookahead principles. (4) Level coverage: beginner (Kian/Donovan tutorials, tutorial.rouxers.com, 4a flowchart), intermediate (SBLP, CMLL recognition, LSE fundamentals, DFDB), advanced (EOLR/EOLRb, F2B inspection planning, misoriented centres, experimental sets). (5) Attribution names for credits screens: Knut Peterson (rouxcubing.com), Zhouheng Sun/onionhoney, Antonio (Anto) Kam, eff, Kian Mansour, Donovan (Lubix), Teoidus, Crys (crystalcuber), Neo (cuar03), Shadowslice, Louis, Jade (enbyne.tech), James Macdiarmid, Athefre, Fengyuan Lou, Jayden McNeill, Fahmi.
